Subject: Post-call: Data handling & logging controls — FintechCo (logging redaction)

Hi Emily / Rajesh,

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation. Quick recap and agreed next steps on the logging / PII topic so we have alignment:

1) What you need:
   - Debuggable request/response traces for incident investigation but no raw PII in logs (names, SSNs, account numbers).
   - Trace IDs that allow you to correlate requests across services without leaking user identifiers.
   - Retention target: 90 days for high-fidelity debug logs; aggregated telemetry longer-term.

2) Redwood options we covered (high-level):
   - Ingest redaction rules (regex + ML PII detection) to mask/hide sensitive fields before storage.
   - Configurable header filtering (e.g., strip Authorization, Cookie headers) and selective retention.
   - Hashing of identifiers (deterministic salted hash) so traces remain correlatable but not reversible.
   - Sampling / truncation to limit full-text retention; option for on-demand retrieval with consent.

3) Open items / asks from FintechCo:
   - Confirm whether deterministic tracing (same trace ID across retries) is required.
   - Examples of fields you consider PII in prompts (we need a short list to tune redaction rules).
   - Any legal/regulatory reqs beyond SOC2 (e.g., specific data residency for logs).

4) Next steps / owners:
   - Dylan to propose a configuration + playbook for masking + examples by EOD Thurs.
   - Monica to bundle our compliance pack (SOC2 + DPA) and share.
   - Marissa (me) to coordinate and confirm timeline for trial environment.

I'll leave Dylan on the thread for the technical follow-up. Thanks — Marissa

--

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A couple clarifications from our side:

- We do need deterministic trace IDs to map across our microservices and support replay for debugging. They must not include any raw user identifiers.
- Our retention policy: 90 days for detailed logs (debug-level) and 2 years for aggregated telemetry. Can you confirm ability to set per-log-type retention?

Hi Emily / Rajesh —

Thanks for the notes. Below is a concrete set of options and constraints so you can pick what fits your risk profile. Happy to jump on a short tech call to walk through examples.

1) Redaction & masking options (pre-storage):
   - Regex + ML-based PII detectors on ingestion pipeline. We apply these to request payloads, response bodies, and header fields. Detected PII can be masked (replaced with ****), removed, or replaced with a deterministic salted hash.
   - Header handling rules: default config strips Authorization, Cookie, and Set-Cookie before persisting. We can also strip any custom header you list.
   - Trace IDs: we generate a random UUID per request by default. For cross-service correlation you can supply your own trace_id in a dedicated header; if you do, we recommend we salt+hash it on ingest to avoid storing raw IDs containing PII.

2) Retention & sampling:
   - Per-log-type retention: yes — you can set retention per stream (debug traces vs metrics).
   - Sampling: you can enable full logging for 100% of requests for a short debug window, then revert to sampled logging (1-5%) with metadata-level events kept at 100%.

3) Access controls & retrieval:
   - Logs encrypted at rest; access gated via RBAC and audit logging.
   - On-demand retrieval workflow: we can retain full debug blobs in a short-term secure store (configurable TTL) that requires a two-person approval for extraction.

4) Practical guidance for your sample prompts:
   - Provide 10-20 representative prompts and highlight fields you consider PII (names, account numbers, full addresses). We'll produce a redaction config and show a before/after sample.

Attachments included: SOC2-TypeII.pdf, FintechCo-DPA-v3.docx.

Proposed next step: I'll draft a redaction config and a runbook (how to enable/disable sampling, how to request retrieval) and share by EOD Thurs.

—Dylan

Subject: Re: Post-call: Data handling & logging controls — FintechCo (logging redaction)

Dylan — thanks for the thorough note. A few technical questions:

- When you say "redact at ingestion", does that mean the original full request is never written to disk? We need certainty that PII is not persisted in any form.
- For hashing identifiers: is the salt managed per-customer (recommended) and can we rotate it? If salted hashing is reversible in any scenario?
- Are trace IDs embedded in any existing fields that could end up in logs (e.g., X-Request-ID including user ids)? We cannot accept trace ids which include any user identifier substring.

Also a reminder: our legal team will require the DPA in our signature packet and confirmation of EU data residency for logs touching EU subjects. We'll share their contact if needed.

Thanks — Rajesh
